chunk_findings.detail: `fingerprint` hashes `load` and `cache` into the key (lines 135-141). These are run-time conditions, not stable machine-class facts. For example, on the same 8-core Linux container with identical `parallel_cap`, `xdist_workers`, Python, ddflow version, and cgroup state, a first sample with `load_ratio=0.20` and a cold cache produces one key; a second sample minutes later with `load_ratio=0.30` and a warm cache produces a different key. The regression detector then cannot compare those samples across commits, contradicting the stated stable-key intent and the docstring’s reason for excluding `git_head`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/env.py:146

chunk_findings.detail: `cgroup_state` claims to read cgroup v1 memory limits but only reads the v1 CPU quota. Given a cgroup v1 memory-limited container where `/sys/fs/cgroup/cpu.max` and `/sys/fs/cgroup/memory.max` are absent, `/sys/fs/cgroup/cpu/cpu.cfs_quota_us` is `-1`, and `/sys/fs/cgroup/memory/memory.limit_in_bytes` is `1073741824`, the function never sees the memory limit; it returns `unlimited` (or `unavailable` if the quota file is also absent), even though the environment is limited.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/env.py:69

chunk_findings.detail: `collect` directly uses external environment/filesystem/git probes (`os.cpu_count`, `os.getloadavg`, `platform.system`, `sys.version`, `Path.exists`/`read_text`, and `head_sha`) inside the service instead of going through ports in `ddflow/adapters`. To test `collect` with a fake deterministic environment, callers must monkeypatch module globals such as `os`, `platform`, `sys`, `__version__`, and `head_sha` rather than pass fake adapters, which is the failure mode [r-adapters] is meant to prevent.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/env.py:170

chunk_findings.detail: The “leaks nothing” assertion is not a sound leak detector because it searches for raw secrets in a JSON-escaped serialization. On Windows, `str(tmp_path)` contains backslashes; if `collect` leaks the path, `json.dumps` emits it as `C:\\Users\\...` (or the leak may use `as_posix()` with forward slashes), so `str(tmp_path) not in blob` is true even though the path is present. The same false pass happens for non-ASCII identifiers: `getpass.getuser() == "José"` is serialized as `Jos\u00e9`, so a leaked username passes the assertion. This can let identifying data ship while the test reports no leak.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_perf_env.py:test_collect_runs_here_and_leaks_nothing

chunk_findings.detail: cgroup_state documents that it reads cgroup v2 then v1 CPU and memory limits, but it never reads the cgroup v1 memory limit file `/sys/fs/cgroup/memory/memory.limit_in_bytes`. On a cgroup v1 host whose memory controller is mounted and capped (e.g. `/sys/fs/cgroup/memory/memory.limit_in_bytes` contains `1073741824`) while the checked v1 CPU quota file `/sys/fs/cgroup/cpu/cpu.cfs_quota_us` is `-1`, this function returns `"unlimited"`; if that CPU file is also absent, it returns `"unavailable"`. Either result misclassifies a memory-limited environment instead of returning `"limited"`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/env.py:cgroup_state

chunk_findings.detail: [r-adapters] This new module directly reaches outside its own process without going through a `ddflow/adapters` port: `_read_file`/`Path.read_text`, `in_container`/`Path.exists`, `cache_state`/`Path.iterdir`, and git via `from ddflow.infra.worktree._merge import head_sha`. A fake git/filesystem backend for tests has no adapter to replace, so the rule’s failure case applies: tests must monkeypatch private modules or stdlib functions instead of swapping one adapter implementation.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/env.py

chunk_findings.detail: `getpass.getuser()` can raise `KeyError` in POSIX containers where the current UID has no `/etc/passwd` entry and none of `LOGNAME`, `USER`, `LNAME`, or `USERNAME` is set (common with arbitrary UIDs, e.g. OpenShift). In that environment this test errors while building the secret list, before it can test anything about the fingerprint.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_perf_env.py:112

chunk_findings.detail: The leak check is not JSON-representation aware: `json.dumps` escapes backslashes as `\\`. On Windows, `str(tmp_path)` and `str(Path.home())` contain single backslashes, so those raw values are not substrings of `blob` even if the fingerprint facts contain the same path in JSON-escaped form. A real path leak on Windows would therefore pass unnoticed.
